about: The rubrics call the sentence before Pater noster the preface of the Lord's Prayer. After et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem, they assign the response sed líbera nos a malo to the server. The same words are also available here as a prayer on their own.

s03.translation: At the Saviour's command and formed by divine teaching, we dare to say:

s04.narrative: The priest spreads his hands, and keeps them so through the prayer.

s05.translation: Our Father, who art in heaven,

s08.translation: Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

s09.translation: Give us this day our daily bread.

s10.translation: And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

s11.translation: And lead us not into temptation,

w004.function: A participle agreeing with the unexpressed nos, the subject of audémus.

w007.function: Ablative of means with formáti. Here institutio means instruction: formed by divine teaching.

w008.function: A participle agreeing with the unexpressed nos, the subject of audémus.

w009.function: “Audémus dícere” expresses filial boldness: instructed by Christ, we dare to say “Our Father.”

w011.function: Vocative singular in direct address to God.

w012.function: Vocative masculine singular agreeing with Pater.

w014.function: After the vocative the relative clause keeps the 2nd person: “who art”, not “who is”.

w016.function: Ablative plural after in. The received English renders it in the singular.

w017.function: Third-person present passive subjunctive expressing a petition.

w019.function: Nominative neuter singular agreeing with nomen.

w020.function: Third-person present active subjunctive expressing a petition.

w022.function: Nominative neuter singular agreeing with regnum.

w023.function: Third-person present subjunctive of fio expressing a petition.

w025.function: Nominative feminine singular agreeing with volúntas.

w033.function: Accusative masculine singular agreeing with panem.

w034.function: Accusative masculine singular agreeing with panem.

w040.function: Dative of the person forgiven with dimítte.

w041.function: Accusative plural. Literally debts. The received English has trespasses.

w042.function: Accusative neuter plural agreeing with débita.

w043.function: Introduces the comparison with our forgiving.

w044.function: Et has the adverbial sense also here.

w046.function: Present indicative, in contrast to the petitionary subjunctives.

w047.function: Dative plural indirect object of dimíttimus. Literally debtors.

w048.function: Dative masculine plural agreeing with debitóribus.

w050.function: Negates the independent subjunctive indúcas to form a prohibition.

w052.function: Second-person present subjunctive in a prohibition with ne.

w053.function: Governs the accusative to express direction into.

w056.function: The embolism that follows begins with the same imperative: Líbera nos, quǽsumus, Dómine.

w059.function: The form can be neuter, evil, or masculine, the Evil One. The following embolism takes it up in the neuter plural: ab ómnibus malis.

w060.function: This Amen is said by the priest.
